title: Ox Alpha offers 100 trillion free tokens a day as open models close on the frontier - TCR 08/24/26
description:
Open-weight models like GLM-5.3 and Kimi K3 closed the capability gap to the closed frontier to 12 points on SemiAnalysis’s composite, an anonymous model called Ox Alpha appeared on OpenRouter with its operator saying it would offer 100 trillion free tokens a day, and Nvidia reportedly warned customers of price hikes above 15% on some next-generation server configurations while committing $6 billion to build its own open-weight model.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-august-24-2026/

0:00 Open and framing
0:40 Open models close the gap as value migrates
4:20 Nvidia's memory bill and open-model bet
7:06 China's robot games
9:39 Two quantum milestones land in one cycle
12:05 The New York Times AI answer layer
14:57 Close

This episode covers the SemiAnalysis open-model gap analysis and the anonymous Ox Alpha drop, Nvidia's memory-driven price hikes and $6 billion Poolside license, China's robot games where a humanoid beat Usain Bolt's time and a rideable robot horse went on sale near $43,000, Japan's Shunkai neutral-atom quantum computer and Brookhaven's 13-mile free-space entanglement link, and the New York Times shipping AI-generated search summaries over its own reporting.

The through-line is where value in AI actually lives. SemiAnalysis found open-weight models now doing some economically valuable coding and agentic work, with the gap on SemiAnalysis’s composite down from 35.8 points to 12.1 and closing, by SemiAnalysis’s definitions, twice as fast each era - then Ox Alpha appeared anonymously and, at a claimed hundred trillion tokens a day, potentially offered more free inference in a day than some startups consume in a year. Nvidia's reported warning of 15%-plus price hikes on some next-generation server configurations traces to memory costs its suppliers control, and its $6 billion bet on an open model reads as a wager that durable value sits in compute and people, not weights it can lease. China's robot games showed a humanoid outrunning Bolt then slamming into a wall without braking first, next to a $43,000 rideable quadruped already shipping. Japan's Shunkai went live at room temperature with a path to 10,000 qubits, and Brookhaven beamed entanglement 13 miles through open air using telescope optics built for the Rubin Observatory. And the New York Times placed an unaudited AI answer layer over 170 years of reporting while its Guild demands mandatory human oversight in writing.
